title: Three Winters and One Short Preface
subtitle: 文学写作 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）
meta: 主题语境：文学写作（人与社会·文学艺术与体育·文学与写作）　|　核心词汇：fiction　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 fiction 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1962 my grandmother ① wrote a fiction that no critic in the town would have reviewed, and she said the writing was the whole of the winter. The ② fiction, meaning the novel itself and not the essay, ran three winters and stayed unread in the book; a fiction, she said, is the only thing in a town that is judged by how long it is left unread.

Every ③ fiction in that town had the same short preface beside it, and the ④ fiction at the far shelf, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A fiction, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to read; my grandmother said the reading is the part that fills three winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the fiction was the whole of the matter, meaning the invention and not the novel. The ⑥ fiction, meaning the invention and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody reads; fiction, he said, is either something you write or the only word that means both a novel and an invention. He said the invention is the part they remember.

By 1969 the ⑦ fiction had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short preface. The ⑧ fiction of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in January, was one town and three winters of reading; fiction, she said, is either the one at the far shelf or the reason you learned to read. She said the reading was never mentioned.

The ⑨ fiction I remember is the one written in the plan, which closed in 1971 and is still described as the quietest in the town. A ⑩ fiction, my mother said in 1973, is the only one that improves by being read; every fiction, she said, is an invention that has agreed to look like a novel. She said the invention was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 小说；虚构作品（指镇上每一部旁边的那一部）
B. n. 小说（指那一部本身，与散文相对）
C. 固定搭配：write a fiction 写一部小说
D. n. 小说（指留给孩子们的那一部）
E. n. 小说（抽象总称，指一个镇上的小说之事）
F. n. 小说（指计划里写到、被人读过的那一部）
G. n. 虚构；编造的事（指一件事里人人都等却无人读到的那样东西）
H. n. 虚构（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人读到的那样东西）

items.q: wrote a fiction that no critic in the town would have reviewed
The fiction, meaning the novel itself and not the essay
the fiction at the far shelf
the fiction was the whole of the matter
the fiction had become a line in a plan
The fiction of the whole thing

answers.why: write a fiction 意为“写一部小说”，1962 年祖母写了一部镇上没有一位评论家肯评的小说。
fiction 意为“小说”，指那一部本身而不是散文，它经过了三个冬天而在簿子上没有被读过。
fiction 意为“小说”，指镇上每一部旁边的那一部，每一部旁边都有同一篇短短的序。
fiction 意为“小说”，指留给孩子们的那一部，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
fiction 意为“虚构、编造的事”，指一件事里人人都等却无人读到的那样东西，叔叔说这桩编造就是那件事的全部。
fiction 意为“虚构”，指人人都等却无人读到的那样东西而不是那一部小说，是事情里人人都等、却无人读到的东西。
fiction 意为“小说”，指计划里写到、被人读过的那一部，到 1969 年这一部成了计划里的一行。
fiction 意为“小说”，祖母一月写道，整件事的小说之事是一个镇子和三个冬天的读过。
fiction 意为“小说”，我记得的是计划里写下的那一部，1971 年结束了，至今仍被说成镇上最安静的一部。
fiction 为抽象总称，母亲 1973 年说，一部小说是唯一会因为被好好读过而变得更好的东西。
